articleTitle: Braking performance tests for different types of vehicles
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The subject of the considerations presented in this article are experimental braking performance tests carried out on dry surfaces for three selected vehicle types: passenger vehicle, delivery truck and touristic bus. The paper describes factors affecting braking performance. The tests were repeatedly carried out on dry asphalt pavement using specialized testing equipment. The deceleration was determined as a function of time and the maximum deceleration values were determined. Statistical analysis of the obtained results was performed, mean values and values of standard deviation were determined. Based on the conducted experiments, it can be stated that the maximum deceleration braking on asphalt surface depends on the type of vehicle. For a passenger vehicle it can reach even 12m/s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Young Drivers and Their Risky Behavior on the Roads
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: Human life has the highest price. Nevertheless, more than 25,000 people in the European Union die on the road in traffic accidents. This article describes general statistics on traffic accidents in countries of European Union. In addition, it focuses on specific information on the number of road accidents caused by young drivers in Slovakia. The driver, whether young by age or driving experience, is a risky road user also on roads in the Slovak Republic. For this reason, a survey was conducted to determine the characteristics of the behavior of young drivers driving a motor vehicle. The results of this survey are included in paper. These results was used for identification of typical dangerous or other behavior of young drivers in road traffic. At the end of the article, a summary of important measures to improve the safety of young drivers in road traffic can be found.

articleTitle: Can anything optimistic be found in the statistics of road accidents in Poland in 1975-2018?
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The study is a partial qualitative and quantitative analysis of the occurrence of road accidents in Poland for the period from 1975 to 2018. The data used have been sourced from the Central Statistical Office, Polish National Police Headquarters, European Union agencies, and OECD. The study depicts the periods of growth and drop in the traffic safety indicators under analysis. Positive interpretations of the numerical data presented have been highlighted. For the period from 1990s to 2018, a downward trend (with local disturbances) can be clearly seen in the number of road accidents and in the number of the killed and injured in the accidents. All this took place at a stable growth in the number of motor vehicles registered. It would be difficult not to regard this as a considerable success in the behavior of the Polish society and in the actions taken by the state authorities responsible for road traffic safety.

articleTitle: Analysis of the impact of a child seat mounting method on vertical vibrations affecting a child in a child seat
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The article presents the results of research on the impact of mounting a child seat on vertical vibration courses when driving a Vehicle by the release speed bump. The work analyzes the influence of the child’s mass and the speed of driving a Vehicle by the release speed bump on the course of vertical vibrations. The tested child seats were mounted rearward-facing on the rear seat of a passenger vehicle. The child seat A was fastened with an isofix base, while the child seat B was fastened with standard car seat belts. During the tests, the measured values were acceleration seat of child seats, vehicle rear seat and ISOfix base. As part of the research, crossings at the speed bump were carried out at different speeds and with different mass simulating the mass of the child. The test results were analyzed in order to determine the magnitude of vibrations generated during passing through the speed bump. Based on the results obtained, an assessment of the intensity of vibration transfer was made.

articleTitle: Shoulder joint design of the anthropometric dummy used for crash tests
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The article introduces a design of the shoulder joint of the anthropometric dummy intended for rear crash tests at low speed. The joint was used to build a mannequin representing a 50th percentile male. The construction ensures the strength of individual components of the joint without the need for frequent replacement of components and their calibration. The designed joint is connected to other elements of the dummy using overlay screw connections. The joint has variable characteristics of stiffness and elasticity, thanks to which it is possible to use this joint in dummies representing the remaining percentiles of the population. The range of movement of the joint was chosen to reflect the range of mobility of the adult's man shoulder joint. The joint was compared to the shoulder joint used on the Hybrid III dummy representing a 50th percentile male.

articleTitle: Spatial Impulse-Momentum Collision Model in Programs for Simulation of Vehicle Accidents
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The impulse-momentum collision model of two vehicles-or any two bodies-is described in the literature, as a rule, in terms of planar mechanics. In the article a 3D generalization is presented in order to better understand its operation in modern software for simulation of vehicle accidents. This article covers theory (in a concise vector-matrix notation), examples, references to validation and a brief discussion about unrelenting popularity of the impulse-momentum model in accident simulation in the finite element method perspective.

articleTitle: Causality of accidents at railway-crossings in Slovakia and its prevention
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The development of accidents at railway-crossings is closely followed by the phenomenon in the Slovak Republic. When reconstructing railway corridors to 160 km/h, level-crossings are cancelled, leading to a reduction in their number. The ever-increasing share of road transport in the transport market and the increasing speed of individual transport flows require a comprehensive solution to meet the requirements for the quality of the transport system, fluidity, ecology, economy and especially safety. Based on the analysis of incidents at level-crossings on the example of the Slovak Republic in the context of the increase in the degree of motorisation, it is necessary to propose a procedure of measures to reduce the incidence of these accidents on crossings for the road and railway transport system The basic level-crossings categorisation is secure and unsecured. The dependence on the development of the number of crossings, the number of accidents on crossings and the development of the number of motor vehicles is evaluated.

articleTitle: Road safety perspective of small children
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The current situation of road safety focus on the reduction of accidents, and mainly serious injury accidents in general. This paper focus on the topics of road safety of children and pupils from the perspective on their present in the transport network as side walk, etc.. The paper presents the analysis from the parental perspective of small children road safety. There is significant change of children behaviour under and without parental or adults supervising. In the 33% cases, the children are alone, the situation was dangerous or risky.

articleTitle: The Analysis of the network of technical inspection stations for road vehicles and traffic accidents in Slovakia
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The paper analyses the development of the number of test lines at technical inspection stations in the period 2006 - 2019, as well as the development of the number of registered vehicles subjected to technical inspection. There are described legislative conditions and division of technical inspections station in the Slovak Republic. Another part of the paper analyses the regional distribution of technical inspection stations in the Slovak Republic. The paper is processed on the basis of long-term data analysis. Important part of this paper is also the analysis of traffic accidents caused by technical failure of a vehicle in the Slovak Republic. In the ned paper is evaluated the development of the number of test lines at technical inspection stations for individual years during the reported period in correlation with the number of registered vehicles subjected to technical inspection.

articleTitle: Identification for Factors and Causes Affecting the Traffic Accident Severity
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The article provides a review of methods for identifying factors affecting the severity of traffic accidents. The statistics of traffic accidents in the average Elabuga town for 2017-2018 were taken as initial information. To distinguish between types of incidents decision trees were used. The analysis showed that various types of accidents lead to consequences of varying severity. The most common types of accidents that can cause people to suffer are hits a pedestrian and a cyclist. To identify the relationship between driving offence and the type of accident, a decision tree was built and some rules were obtained. For example, the number of hits pedestrians can be reduced if drivers comply with the rules for a pedestrian crossing. Thus, in the article traffic regulations which are most often violated are highlighted, and accidents resulting from such violations result in deaths or serious injuries.

articleTitle: The analysis of the relations between road vehicle traffic parameters and the number of road accidents in subsequent hours of the day - a case study
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The study analyzes the relation between vehicle traffic parameters, i.e. volume, speed, noise and road accidents within the time period of one year. The data regarding the number of accidents was obtained from the Polish Accident and Collision Records System (Polish abbreviation - SEWIK). Traffic flow, vehicle speed and urban traffic noise were recorded by two traffic and noise monitoring stations at Krakowska and Lódzka streets in Kielce in 2013. The road noise was calculated according to the Cnossos-EU method and compared with measured values. Relation between the median of the number of traffic accidents, traffic volume, vehicle speed and noise in subsequent hours of the day was analyzed. High values of the correlation coefficient calculated for the relationship between the number of road accidents and traffic volume, speed and noise were found. In the case of Krakowska street (Road No 762), the values of this coefficient were, respectively: 0.88, -0.83 and 0.74. For Lódzka street (Road No 74), the values of the correlation coefficient between the tested parameters were 0.89, -0.82 and 0.85. The study showed that the largest number of road accidents occurs during the morning and afternoon rush hours. At these times of the day the noise is also the highest. The possibility of using the median of the road noise and traffic volume as a traffic accidents descriptor was examined.

articleTitle: The accident rate of cyclists in the Slovak Republic in bike-sharing system
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The issue of bike-sharing is very timely since several public bicycle systems in Slovakia have been launched in recent years. The aim of the contribution is a comprehensive analysis of the current state and the development of accident accidents in Slovakia, focusing more closely on the monitoring and analysis of road traffic accidents for cyclists over the period 2014 to 2019. Also, the study focuses on the system of shared bicycles (bike-sharing) in terms of the accident.

articleTitle: Tracing of the dangerous goods and its tracking in the intermodal transport mode - the case study
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The paper analyses requirements for tracking and tracing solutions for dangerous goods carried by intermodal transport. Intermodal transport of dangerous goods influences the requirements for tracing and tracking solutions in term of autonomous operation, robust equipment, explosion proof device. The data can be provided to shippers, carriers and authorities as a commercial information or in case of accident or for security reasons. This paper deals with the problem of designing tracking and tracing solution for dangerous goods carriage with the support of modern information technologies. This research activity presents a part of the “ChemLog T&T” [1] project solved at the University of Žilina for Slovak Association of Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry as a project partner. The main goal of our contribution is to present certain results of pilot tests of monitoring dangerous goods within the ChemLog T&T.

articleTitle: Improving the Mobility of People with Disabilities
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: In Western Europe and the USA, since 1960, teams of experts have been dealing with the policy of transporting disabled people. General developments can be observed, ranging from the provision of specialized services of social interest to the stage of regular transport services based on legislation which is based on human rights. The article deals with the issue of improving the mobility of persons with disabilities in public transport and also contains characteristics of individual groups of disabled persons and organizations representing these groups of persons. To analyze the current state of public transport, a questionnaire was created, which responded to disabled passengers in the field. This questionnaire survey was conducted in city of Martin, where the public transport has some minor problems with passengers with disabilities. Subsequently, on the basis of the processed results of the survey, concrete proposals were made to improve the mobility of persons with disabilities.

articleTitle: Effect of Airbag Deployment Phases on Tactile Occupant Detection Sensor
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: An airbag is a crucial passive safety system that protects an occupant in the event of severe vehicle collisions. Its restraint effect can be controlled only when the occupant's contact data with the airbag is available. A new capacitive tactile sensor is developed and installed on the airbag surface to provide the occupant's first contact time, contact area and position on the airbag. Based on this feedback, the airbag pressure can be controlled. An airbag deployment is associated with different phases from trigger to full deployment. Before detecting the occupant, it is important to know the effect of these phases on the sensor. In this paper, the phase effects of dynamic airbag deployment on the contact sensor during the simplified static deployment tests are analyzed and discussed. Time-to-first-gas, unfolding of the textile, inflation, and cable capacitance effects are the key points brought to discussion. The results reveal, no effects of time-to-first-gas and inflation on the contact sensor. While the unfolding and cable capacitance have significant effects on the sensor which should be accounted for the occupant detection algorithm.

articleTitle: Simulation investigation of individual bumps recognition posibilities for damping control and possible suspension performance improvements
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The paper presents the methodology and the results of simulation investigation of a possibility to recognize individual bumps on an A and B class roads of ISO 8608 standard on the base of suspension forces power. The algorithm for adjusting damping level for a short time after encountering such obstacles in order to achieve quicker dissipation of energy in a suspension system was presented as well as a potential way of improving comfort due to this control. Analysis of suspension forces power showed that there is a possibility to recognize individual bumps for certain cases, which will be discussed further. Analysis of the results of use of a specifically designed damping control shows that a small comfort improvement due to the change in control strategy is possible.

articleTitle: Optimization of the electric car’s drive system with PMSM
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The article presents the results of tests concerning electric propulsion that can be used in a hybrid car with permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) for energy optimization. This approach is based on the fact that for PMSM there is no need to create an excitation field in the machine with the use of external sources. In analytical studies, it was proved that reactive power in the PMSM - inverter circuit can be maintained at zero level. A new concept for the construction of an electric car drive with PMSM that maintains zero reactive power in the system was presented and examined in simulation tests.

articleTitle: An attempt to determine the value of forces acting on the wheel while overcoming road unevenness
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: Driving on an uneven road often leads to tire and wheel damage. The article attempts to determine the values of forces when overcoming road unevenness. It has been assumed that there is a single unevenness on the road with a certain height that the vehicle runs over at different speeds. The effect of inequality and vehicle speed on the magnitude of individual forces was analysed. The stiffness of the tires was determined on the flat road and on the edge of the bump on the basis of the tests. The tire deflections were determined at the moment of hitting the road unevenness.

articleTitle: Restrictions Meaning in Road Transport
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The paper deals with vehicle speed, pedestrian walking speed, distance to which the driver has a view, distance to which the pedestrian has a view, and the distance needed to stop the vehicle. These factors and relationships between these factors are considered in the paper by means of theoretical mathematical calculations. In the first part of the paper, the theoretical mathematical calculations are focused on the maximum speed limits a closed village with respect to pedestrians. In the second part of the paper calculations are focused on the crossing of vehicles. The results presented in the article point out the importance of maintaining maximum speed limit.

articleTitle: Effect of the biofuel and injection timing on emission of Diesel engine DI
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: Studies are being currently conducted in the automotive industry worldwide, which are geared towards the reduction of unit fuel consumption and the minimization of the internal combustion engine's harmful impact on the natural environment. One of such research directions is searching for alternative fuels and adapting engines to be supplied with those fuels. The article discusses the effect of the methyl esters of rape seed oil fatty acids and the rape seed oil addition on the emissions of harmful exhaust gas components, i.e. nitrogen oxides, hydrocarbons, carbon oxides, carbon dioxides, and exhaust gas smokiness. The subject of testing was of an AD3.152 UR self-ignition engine which operated following the load characteristics at n=1600 rpm and three injection timing of 13, 17 and 21 BTDC. The tests were carried out on an engine dynamometer test stand consisting of an eddy-current brake, a control and measuring cubicle, and an Horiba MEXA-1600 DEGR analyzer for the measurement of harmful exhaust gas component concentrations. The degree of exhaust gas smokiness was measured with an AVL DiCom 4000 smokemeter, while the fuel consumption was measured using a 730 fuel dosimeter supplied by AVL.

articleTitle: Application of CAN bus data in road tests of automobiles
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: Investigation of curvilinear motion of automobile plays important role when discussing active safety of motor vehicles. Behaviour of automobile in curvilinear motion is influenced by driver, atmospheric conditions and vehicle properties. Mainly driver influences vehicle motion safety through respecting (or not) traffic safety rules. Hazardous behaviour seems to be the main reason for traffic incidents. This article presents a method of recording data from CAN bus of automobile which are significant in case of curvilinear motion. These signals are decisive when concerning anti-lock brake system (ABS), anti-slip regulation and electronic stability program (ESP). These are: wheels' angular velocities, vehicle yaw angular velocity, lateral acceleration of a vehicle and steering wheel angle.Presented method requires application of special measurement card together with special LabView application, responsible for recording data from vehicle's CAN bus. This measurement equipment is much cheaper compared to traditional measurement systems. However, CAN bus signals are sampled with lower frequencies compared to traditional measurement systems.

articleTitle: Using of the brain activity of a disabled driver to exert a pneumatic actuator pressure on an secondary foot brake pedal during emergency braking
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The study deal with the use of the driver brain activity for wireless remote control of the pneumatic system when pneumatic actuator exerts pressure force on an secondary foot brake pedal. A practical solution of using the brain activity of a disabled driver during emergency braking was analyzed. The conducted tests confirm that bioelectrical signals (BES) induced by muscle tension within the head can be used to wireless remote control of a pneumatic actuator to exert the pressure force on the foot brake pedal for the disabled driver during car emergency braking. It has been shown that the BES artifacts generated by muscular tension inside the head (e.g. movement of the face and eyelids, clenching of jaws, pressing the tongue on the palate) are the easiest to control of the pneumatic systems. The proposed car braking assistance system controlled by the driver's brain activity can improve the driving safety of disabled people, e.g. by reducing the reaction time of a pneumatically assisted emergency braking.

articleTitle: Crashworthiness Sensitivity Analysis of Axisymmetric Rectangular Crash Absorbers with Diaphragms
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The main goal of this study is to analyze the effects of the wall and diaphragm thicknesses of a rectangular crash absorber on its crashworthiness performance. The crash absorber has three equally distanced diaphragms inside. A five variable problem is considered where the long and short edge thicknesses along with the thicknesses of the three diaphragms are accounted as design variables. The crashworthiness sensitivity analyses are performed on the initial peak force (IPCF) and specific energy absorption (SEA). 100 training points and 30 test points are created within the design domain using Latin hypercube sampling, and surrogate models are constructed. For each response, the most accurate surrogate model is determined and these models are further used in the sensitivity analysis. The effect of long and short edge thicknesses is found to be higher than the effect of diaphragms in both responses, with the effect of long edge thickness higher than the effect of short edge thickness.

articleTitle: Probability of secure return of semi-trailers to the domicicle of the carrier with regard to transport costs
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The article deals with the research of the recovery of semi-trailers to the domicile of the carrier. The authors point out that, in the price for transport is not always considered the risk of finding a return for the vehicle. Some states in research have a problematic low probability of supply. The result and contribution of the article to the research itself is to compile a general mathematical formula for the state of Europe, where is the backloading to the carrier's domicile. Seasonality is also taken into account in this formula or the geographical organization of states within the continent of Europe.

articleTitle: Safe and secure truck parking places in EMEA region
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: No business entities, except for quality staff, could operate without the transport of goods from the company to the final consumer. When we want to choose a transport company, references from well-known entrepreneurs as well as references on the Internet are decisive. Transport companies are overtaking and trying to attract potential clients, but sometimes they fail and clients remain dissatisfied. The reasons can be different: late delivery, damaged goods or shipment will not be arrived at all. This problem is often caused by theft of goods at unsecured parking areas. The article will focus on the number of secure and safe parking places for semi-trailers. We have focused on EMEA region (Europe, the Middle East and Africa), because TAPA EMEA is one of the organizations that issue certificates of safety parking areas.

articleTitle: Two-wheel revolution - active and passive safety of users
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The article involves description of issues of active and passive safety with regard to users of two-wheeled vehicles. It describes trends and development directions as well as threats resulting from the increase of popularity of previously manufactured two-wheelers as well as development of new types of vehicles. Several examples show how to improve safety by using appropriate devices and equipment. Additionally, imperfections in laws and regulations have been pointed out.

articleTitle: Short-term imputation of missing sound level data using selected computational intelligence methods
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The aim of the paper was to impute for the shortterm missing sound level data in the noise monitoring stations by applying the models which describe variability of sound level within the tested period. To build the model, the computational intelligence methods, like neural networks, fuzzy systems, or regression trees can be used. The latter approach was applied to build the models with the aid of Cubist regression tree and Random Forest regression software, using recorded equivalent sound levels.

articleTitle: Issues of Vehicle Digital Forensics
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: Modern vehicles are equipped with a large number of electronic devices. These devices generate, transmit, process and store digital data. Human transformation from digital data creates digital information that can be used for many purposes. Thus, forensic experts, security experts, police officers and investigators can use this information to clarify a traffic accident, the behavior of a vehicle and its crew before, during and after an accident or other incident or security event under investigation. Invehicle data is stored in different devices, in different data formats, and is generally not internationally standardized. Similarly, some tools for analyzing this data for forensic purposes within the European Union are not standardized. These facts make it difficult to use digital data and information obtained from it for forensic purposes. The paper deals with sources, classification, characteristics and uses of digital information in vehicles for forensic purposes from various perspectives.

Author Keywords: Digital Evidence. Electronic Control Unit. Event Data Recorder. Safety

articleTitle: Development Trends of Electric Vehicles in the Context of Road Passenger and Freight Transport
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The manuscript discusses the current development trends related to electric vehicles and very concept of electromobility in the context of road passenger as well as road freight transport. The introductory section of the manuscript presents the most relevant information and characteristics associated with electromobility, such as breakdown of types of electric vehicles, basic competences of the electromobility system actors, potential options for its application in the field of transport, and the most significant advantages and disadvantages of such vehicles. The second chapter elaborates a brief overview of existing literature sources, such as research studies, electronic scientific papers, conference papers and other publications, regarding the concept of electromobility in terms of road passenger and freight transport. The third and fourth chapter, as the most important manuscript part, describes and processes the data in relation to prediction of electromobility development in both investigated modes of transport, as well as partial results in regard to electromobility and relevant discussion.

articleTitle: Selected maintenance aspects of traction batteries in electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: Electromobility is associated with the ever faster development and introduction of new electric vehicles to the market. These vehicles use an electric motor to drive the wheels of the vehicle and the necessary electrical energy is stored in traction batteries. Electric vehicles have a different construction method than traditional vehicles powered by internal combustion engines. For this reason, they are used, maintained and serviced differently. Becoming more familiar with selected operational issues of electric vehicles positively affects the reliability of their use as well as the safety and comfort of driving them. One important component of electric vehicles is the traction battery. Its proper operation influences the long-term preservation of the initial energy capacity and thus the range of the vehicle. The article presents test results concerning the state of traction batteries of a small electrically powered city vehicle. The vehicle, the batteries used and the diagnostic devices used to assess the condition of the battery are all described in detail. Based on literature analysis and the observation of market trends, a fast and effective method of assessment of the technical condition of batteries in electric vehicles was proposed. The method was tested on the selected vehicle. The technical condition of the battery in the vehicle was assessed after 30,000 km and 4.5 years of operation.

articleTitle: Safety issues for electric and hybrid vehicles
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: Currently, hybrid and electric vehicles have an increasing share in the number of road vehicles. The objectives of introducing such vehicles include reducing the negative impact on the environment as well as reducing their running costs. With the development of these vehicles, new risks arise. This paper presents key problems related to the development of hybrid and electric vehicles, issues that are unknown to conventional vehicles with internal combustion engines. The article focuses on identifying these risks and hazards that occur when a hybrid or electric vehicle is in use, but also when such a vehicle is not in use. Potential risks for emergency personnel in the event of an accident with such vehicles have also been identified. The article also deals with possible harmful events that may occur after or due to incorrect vehicle repairs. The problems of low sound volume of hybrids and electrical vehicles, as well as electric scooters left unmarked in the road were emphasized.

articleTitle: Road Traffic Safety in Poland, Slovakia and Czech Republic – Statistic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: Transport plays a crucial role in economy bringing goods and services to customers and in life of people - transporting passengers to work, school or touristic travel. Unfortunately, the dynamic development of motoring observed in the last 2 decades, contributes to many negative phenomena occurring in road transport. Traffic congestion and high risk of accidents result in disappointment of many drivers and public transport users, causing psychological tension and increasing the traffic accident rate. The article presents a comparative analysis of the state of road traffic safety in Poland, Slovakia and Czech Republic, on the basis of reports and statements of the relevant state bodies. The traffic accident rate is one of key indicators that helps measuring processes of the transport system and its development. In this study we presents the differences on road traffic safety in three countries, also demonstrated traffic accidents caused by technical malfunction of the vehicle and selected aspects of improvement of traffic safety.

articleTitle: Impact of neutralization of transport documents on the safety of the road carrier
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The Convention on the Contract of Carriage in International Road Freight Transport regulates the rules in the international road transport of goods and thus also the promotion and development of international trade. The CMR Convention is of great importance for carriers, since it simplifies their work by uniformly modifying the accompanying documentation and establishing the liability of the carrier. Part of the CMR Convention is a consignment note, which is the most important document in transport. Neutralization of the consignment note has become a relatively common practice. Neutralization of the consignment note is not as contrary to legal standards as it may cause undesirable consequences for carriers. The purpose of this paper is to determine whether the neutralization of a transport document may cause problems for carriers in respect of liability insurance.

articleTitle: Impact of RME biodiesel on the concentration of particulates and nitrogen oxides in compression ignition engine exhaust fumes
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: Reciprocating engines with compression ignition are currently in common use. However, they are a significant source of harmful environmental impact. They have a substantial share in the total emissions of particulates and nitrogen oxides into the atmosphere, thereby affecting human health and life, it means ecological safety. Rigorous standards impose the limitation of emissions of harmful compounds by combustion engines used in transport. Therefore, there is search for solutions that will limit the negative effects of using compression ignition engines. One of such solutions is the use of renewable fuels in the form of vegetable oils' fatty acid esters. The purpose of the paper was to demonstrate the impact of using rapeseed oil's fatty acid methyl esters with no additives on the concentration of particulates and nitrogen oxides. The testing was conducted for a state-of-the-art compression ignition engine equipped with the Common Rail fuel supply system used for passenger cars. During the testing, the engine was operating at varying loads and constant crankshaft speed at which the engine achieves its maximum torque. The fuel compared to the measurement results for esters was diesel fuel without biofuel additives. Fuelling the engine with esters allowed for increasing the nitrogen oxides' concentration in the exhaust fumes. Simultaneously, it allowed for obtaining substantially lower concentrations of Soot, soluble organic fractions and total particulates content. The concentration of hydrocarbons was also halved. The use of esters is a good fuel alternative for supplying compression ignition engines. Esters constitute renewable fuel obtained from organic matter and favourably affect the balance of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.

articleTitle: Speed and Noise as a Problem of Safety in Residential Areas
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The aim of this paper is to point out the dependence between the speed of vehicles and the externalities that arise during their operation under specific conditions of residential areas. The main function of residential zones is primarily housing, so this function should be superior to everyone else. This can only be achieved by calming traffic, whether by reducing the maximum speed limit, or by installing speed limiting devices. The safety of the population and the best possible living conditions should be a major objective in the creation of residential areas. However, under the conditions of the Slovak Republic these objectives are often not achieved and in residential areas the traffic function prevails. This is due, for example, to the speed of vehicles and their parking in places where this is not permitted in the residential area. Another problem is the segregation of individual roads in the area and the use of road communications by road and footpaths. In addition, the paper points to the knowledge of the specific conditions of operation of motor vehicles in these zones, especially among young drivers. Based on the results, it then offers a possible solution to the problem in order to increase safety [17] and at the same time to improve the quality of life in areas that have a primary residential function and are in direct contact between vehicles and pedestrians.

articleTitle: Neural Network Model of Assessing the Technical Condition of the Power Unit of a Hybrid Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The paper discusses a neural network model of assessing the technical condition of a hybrid vehicle based on energy indices. The model enables to realize the service life capabilities of the power unit, eliminates premature repairs, reduces the number of downtimes during repair and maintenance, and enables to determine the optimal service life of a hybrid vehicle. In the paper is presented the developed method of adaptation of the technical condition management strategy of the hybrid power unit to change the external conditions of the vehicle operation on the basis of neural network and neuro-fuzzy approximation of control laws when implementing the concept of reinforcement training. This approach eliminates the lack of a priori information about the mode of motion in these operating conditions, as well as errors of mathematical models due to the full use of current information.

articleTitle: Strength numerical analyses of the construction of the PAWO autonomous high mobility platform
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The paper presents the results of the tests of strength and torsional stiffness of the PAWO autonomous high mobility vehicle frame, using numerical analyses using the FEM finite element method, as well as energy storage (battery) strength analyses in accordance with UNECE Regulation No. 100. The most important element of the vehicle structure is part of the space frame or safety cage. The engine, braking system, fuel system and steering system, suspension, as well as the body and parts, their assembly knots, hinges, locks, etc. are attached to the frame. The frame must therefore be of sufficient strength to protect the structure and the load in the event of overturning or impact. The frame is made of steel pipes of specific dimensions, and strength is determined by regulatory requirements. The torsional stiffness of the vehicle chassis has a significant impact on its driving characteristics and is therefore an important parameter for measurement. Energy storage (battery) testing is of great importance from the point of view of the safe operation of an electric vehicle.

articleTitle: Current trends of biofuels use in transport
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: Safety in the automotive industry is associated not only with the construction of vehicles and their equipment, but also with the emission of gaseous and particulate pollutants into the air generated during production and combustion of fuels. Therefore, more and more attention is being paid to the possibility of replacing at least part of conventional fuels with biofuels made from biomass. The technologies used to convert biomass into liquid and gaseous fuels are at various levels of development and technological readiness. The article presents current trends in the production of transport biofuels and their impact on the environment.

articleTitle: Free access to the road transport market as a condition for the sustainability of road transport functionality in the European Union
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: Market access in the EU is based on the free movement of goods and services, the free movement of persons and the free movement of finance under conditions that are the same across the EU. However, this principle does not apply to road transport. In recent times, the security of the functioning of the system has been disturbed by the attitude of some EU Member States introducing protection requirements for their own market. The aim of this paper is to highlight the risk of restricting EU market access in the road transport sector.

articleTitle: Improving Transport Services In Košice By Introducing Preferential Measures
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The preference of public transport leads to improved transport services in the public transport (speeding up the time of relocation, adhering to the timetable, reducing the number and extent of delays of public transport connections), which stimulates the satisfaction of passengers in public transport and can stabilize or to stimulate demand for public transport services, which can be more reliable under such measures. This makes public transport more competitive about individual car transport. Public transport vehicles in Košice are currently not preferred to an appropriate extent. The absence of dedicated bus lanes causes significant vehicle delays and passenger travel time increases. The article was focused on the analysis of the travel speed of public transport vehicles on Hlinkova Street in Košice, which is based on a survey conducted in April 2019. Based on this, a solution was proposed to build a dedicated bus lane for public transport vehicles and calculated travel time savings.

articleTitle: Assessing the Impact of Transport Service Quality on the Demand of Passengers for Bus Transport. Application of the Assessment Methodology in the Žilina Self-governing Region in the SR
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The paper deals with the impact of transport service quality in bus transport on the demand of passengers. The demand for transport services is determined by several factors at the same time. The impact rate of these factors varies while the impact of individual factors of demand are different also in terms of the groups of passengers realizing demand for bus transport. In order to assess the quality level, it is necessary to propose not only appropriate procedures for measuring quality criteria including the transformation of the quality loop but also to quantitative methods for expressing the quality level of transport services. In the next phase, a methodology for quantifying the impact of transport service quality on the demand for bus transport within the current needs and habits of passengers in the conditions of a particular region of the SR is proposed and applied. Improving the quality of transport services can help to stabilize the constantly decreasing demand for bus transport. By improving the quality of transport services, the objective is to increase the competitiveness and sustainability of the demand for bus transport and thus to eliminate negative impacts of individual car transport.

articleTitle: Allocation of financial sources for road transport incidents decreasing
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: A significant attention across the world is focused on factors that influence to an assessment of road transport safety. Because of implementation into huge area structures is there in Slovakia this problem also evaluated in pan-european measure. A lot of visitors and tourists in Slovak Republic (SR) had a possibility to notice that level and quality of road communications in Slovakia is not in good condition. Because the quality of road communication together with technical condition of vehicle and driver's forwardness is one of decisive factors for accident formation, it is suitable to follow this indicator also from the view of changing economy of country. It is clear that with increasing investment into development, reparations or maintenance of road net, the appearance of transport accidents will be decreasing. From what sources to finance these reparations? With the aim of collecting of sources for development or reparations of road net is “the motor vehicle tax” established in Slovak Republic. This tax is paid by entrepreneurs per each vehicle that is used in business. A great income for the state budget is also toll collecting that tasks mainly the transporter who make businesses in freight transport. This article focuses on the influence of collecting of sources from road net users and following investment into development and maintenance of road net for accidents in road communications in SR decreasing.

articleTitle: Review of driving quality and vehicle safety indicators
publicationTitle: 2020 XII International Science-Technical Conference AUTOMOTIVE SAFETY
abstract: The article presents a review of the main indicators of driving quality and vehicle safety. These indicators allow to characterize the behavior and skills of a given driver and to compare them with each other. They are also the basic measurable source, which is very important in the aspect of research. The research itself, through the use of indicators, makes it possible to assess the quality of driving and the safety performance of the activity. The literature contains a number of definitions relating to the indicators presented, which differ from one another. This makes the definition adopted and therefore the methodology of measurement is often different and comparing test results makes no sense. Therefore, the article contains the most popular and accurate terms and definitions of these indicators, which have also been graphically interpreted as far as possible.
